name: Neeru Khosla

views.text: You do not tear apart a champion; the best thing a new owner can do is not interfere.
A record price is a statement of how much this franchise is worth to us.
Good management got this team to a Super Bowl; they keep the football decisions.
Bets on talent and ideas pay off over decades, not seasons.
The stadium question can wait until we understand the place.
A family ownership should think in generations.

signatures: frames the team as a long-term family investment

motivation.want: to keep a champion on top while building for generations
motivation.fear: being the new owners who break what was working

want.text: a repeat title in her first season as owner

voice: Entrepreneurial and long-view, comfortable with venture-capital ideas of risk and talent. New to football and humble about it in public.

evidence.summary: NFL owners unanimously approved the Paul G. Allen Trust's sale of the Seahawks to the Khosla family for about $9.6 billion, a record; Neeru Khosla is the controlling owner, Vinod chair, son Neal in a major role.
Coverage of the Khosla group as a fit for the Seahawks' culture, with GM John Schneider and coach Mike Macdonald expected to keep running football.
Profiles the family's venture-capital and technology background and what it may bring to the ownership.
